prerequisites: The mathematical content of secondary school programs.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide fundamental concepts, with a view to applications, related to infinitesimal, differential and integral calculus for real functions of a real variable; acquire adequate logical formalization skills and conscious operational ability.

The student must demonstrate knowledge of the notions (definitions, statements, demonstrations if foreseen by the program) relating to infinitesimal, differential, and integral calculus for real functions of a real variable and the calculation tools developed, and be able to understand related topics by processing the acquired notions.

Finally, the student must demonstrate the ability to apply what has been learned in solving verification exercises prepared by the Lecturer, generally linked to topics such as: existence fields, limits of sequences and functions, numerical series, function studies, definite and indefinite integration.

syllabus_topics: Numerical sets - Natural, integer, rational numbers. The axioms of real numbers. Supremum, infimum, maximum, minimum. Archimedes' principle. Density of Q in R; n-th root; power with real exponent (s.d.). Principle of induction. Bernoulli's inequality. Binomial formula.

Sequences - Limit of a sequence; first properties of limits: uniqueness of limit, comparison, permanence of sign theorems. Operations with limits and indeterminate forms. Monotonic sequences: regularity theorem; the number e. Ratio test. Root test. Theme of arithmetic mean and geometric mean. Ratio-root test. Cauchy's convergence criterion. Subsequences. Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem.

Numerical series - Definitions and first properties; operations with series. Geometric series, harmonic series and generalized harmonic series. Cauchy's criterion for series. Series with non-negative terms: root, ratio, comparison, asymptotic comparison, infinitesimals criteria. Euler-Mascheroni constant. Alternating series: Leibniz criterion; remainder estimation. Absolutely convergent series and their properties.

Functions - Topology of the real line: accumulation points, closed sets, open sets, compact sets. Limits of functions and their properties. Equivalent definition of limit. Operations with limits and indeterminate forms. Monotonic functions: regularity theorems; continuous functions; Lipschitz functions; inverse functions; composite functions. Limit of a composite function. Absolute extrema: Weierstrass theorem. Zero theorem, intermediate value theorem. Uniformly continuous functions, Cantor's theorem.

Differential calculus - Definition of derivative and its geometric meaning. Differentiation rules; derivatives of elementary functions. Relative extrema: necessary first-order condition. Rolle's and Lagrange's theorems; characterization of monotonic functions in intervals. Relative extrema: sufficient first-order conditions. Theorem on the extendability of the derivative. First de L'Hôpital's theorem; second de L'Hôpital's theorem; calculation of limits that appear in indeterminate form. Infinitesimals and infinites: cancellation principles. Taylor's formula with remainder in Peano form. Taylor's formula with remainder in Lagrange form. Overview of Taylor series. Relative extrema: necessary and sufficient second-order conditions. Geometric meaning of the second derivative. Convexity and concavity in an interval; characterization of convex functions in intervals; inflection points; asymptotes; graphs of functions.

Integral calculus - Overview of Peano-Jordan measure. Riemann integral of a bounded function in a compact interval. Area of the curvilinear trapezoid. Integrability of monotonic functions in compact intervals. Integrability of continuous functions in compact intervals. Properties of the definite integral. Mean value theorem for integrals. Fundamental theorem of integral calculus. Primitives and indefinite integration. Rules of indefinite integration: decomposition into sum, integration by parts, integration by substitution, integration of rational functions. Generalization of the concept of integral: summability. Summability criteria.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. The written questions can be multiple choice, open-ended, and numerical exercises.
